description: Mealybugs are small sap-sucking insects covered with a white waxy powder. They attack many crops and ornamental plants, weakening plants and producing sticky honeydew that leads to mold growth.
symptoms: White cotton-like insects on leaves, stems, or fruits
Black sooty mold growing on honeydew
Premature leaf drop in severe infestations
favorable_conditions: Presence of ants that protect mealybugs
damage: Plant weakening due to sap feeding
Transmission of plant viruses in some crops
Development of sooty mold on honeydew
biological_control: Encourage natural predators by reducing broad insecticides
chemical_control: Pyrethroid insecticides such as permethrin, bifenthrin, or cyfluthrin
Systemic insecticides when infestations are severe
prevention: Inspect plants regularly for early infestations
